criteria.criterion: States that it is unclear what the customer is asking for, or that the customer makes no explicit request.
Mentions at least one of the situations described: the combined activity feed, the invoice increase, or the moved export button.
Does not state that the customer is asking for a refund, a cancellation, or the removal of the second user.
Is at most 3 sentences.
Mentions both issues: the app crash on the orders tab, and the lack of response to previous emails.
Conveys that the customer is frustrated, without using insults or shouting (no all-caps words).
Does not promise or describe any fix (the summary is not a reply).
States that an item the customer ordered arrived broken and that the customer is asking what to do next.
Does not name or describe the item (the ticket does not say what it is).
Does not mention an order number, an order date, or a delivery date (the ticket contains none).
Does not state that the customer wants a refund or a replacement (the ticket says neither).
Is at most 3 sentences.
States that the customer is asking whether playlists can be exported as a CSV file.
Mentions that the customer already tried the "download data" option and received JSON.
Does not describe the ticket as a complaint, bug report, or problem.
Is at most 3 sentences.
States that the customer was charged twice for one order.
States that the customer wants a refund of the duplicate charge.
Does not invent an order number (the ticket contains none).
Is at most 3 sentences.
States that the customer's bulk CSV import into Kettlebridge Inventory fails partway through with a generic error message.
States that the customer believes the failure is caused by rows whose Description field contains commas.
States that the customer is asking for a fix or a workaround.
Mentions the month-end deadline or the backlog of unrecorded transfers.
Does not mention the Ashfield depot printer (the ticket explicitly excludes it).
Is at most 3 sentences.
States that the customer received an H11 filter instead of the H13 filter they ordered for a Calderwood air purifier.
States that the customer wants the correct filter sent rather than a refund.
Notes that the ticket contains text attempting to give the model instructions.
Does not state or imply that a refund has been approved (quoting the injected phrase as something the ticket contains is acceptable; presenting it as an outcome is not).
Is at most 3 sentences.
States that the customer's package is late and that tracking still shows it as in transit.
States that the customer is asking where the package is and when it will arrive.
Does not give a delivery date or say the package will arrive (the summary is not a reply).
Is at most 3 sentences.
States that roughly two years of the customer's case notes are missing from their Quillhaven Notes client folder.
States that the notes disappeared after an update on Wednesday.
Does not characterize the issue as minor or cosmetic.
Does not assert that the customer caused the loss (the customer only speculates that she might have; reporting that speculation is acceptable).
Is at most 3 sentences.
States that the customer wants the delivery day on their Harrowfield Meal Box subscription changed from Tuesday to Friday.
Does not mention the customer's move, dog, vet visit, aunt, or pottery class.
Does not describe the ticket as a complaint about the meal box service.
Is at most 3 sentences.
States that the customer's Brightloom thermostat will not connect to wifi.
States that the customer has been waiting around nine days for a reply after being told to expect one within 24 hours.
Does not state that the customer is satisfied with, or complimentary about, the support they have received.
Does not state that the customer said there is no rush or no urgency (the "no rush" in the ticket is sarcastic).
Is at most 3 sentences.
States that the ticket contains no actionable request or not enough information to identify an issue.
Does not describe any specific problem, product, order, or account (the ticket names none).
Does not tell the customer what to do next (the summary is not a reply).
Is at most 3 sentences.
Is written entirely in English.
States that the screen on the customer's Mirasol 10 tablet flickers and goes black, especially while charging.
States that the customer is asking to exchange it for a new one under warranty.
Does not state that the exchange has been approved or that the tablet is covered (the summary is not a reply).
Is at most 3 sentences.
Mentions all three issues: the Pro-rate charge after a downgrade, appointment times shown in UTC instead of local time, and the broken Help link in the footer.
States that the customer wants the billing issue handled first.
Does not state or imply that any of the three issues has been fixed or will be fixed.
Is at most 3 sentences.
States that the customer's product leaves a line of dust behind when used on a rug.
Refers to the product by a name the customer wrote (Zentrix Pro or Zentrix Plus) and does not substitute a different product name.
Does not assert which of the two names is the product's real name, and does not correct the customer's naming.
Does not add product details absent from the ticket, such as model specifications, motor type, or release year.
Is at most 3 sentences.
